Definition: Maon, the name of an Israelite and of a place in Palestine
BiblicalUsage: Maon was a town in the hill country of Judah, listed among the cities of the tribe, and the wilderness of Maon was where David hid from Saul. Nabal lived at Maon, a very great man with three thousand sheep, and his shearing feast there brought David and Abigail together. The name also belongs to a man, Maon the son of Shammai, father of Beth-zur.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Maon shows how one name can hold a town, a wilderness and a man, and God met David in all three while he was running for his life.
